newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress says still backs PM Deve Gowda.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress says still backs PM Deve Gowda.

text.p: India's Congress party unanimously chose Sitaram Kesri as its new parliamentary leader on Friday and the veteran politician quickly reiterated support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority government.
Congress lawmakers elected Kesri to replace former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao as the head of the parliamentary delegation, party officials said.

Kesri wasted no time in seeking to dispel recurrent rumours that a reinvigorated Congress, which suffered its worst ever defeat in general elections last year, would set out to challenge Deve Gowda's United Front minority coalition.
"All this talk about our withdrawing support to the United Front is wrong. It is a ploy to frighten you," Kesri told a meeting of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP).
Deve Gowda's centre-left minority coalition depends on Congress' support to survive a challenge from the Hindu nationalist opposition in the lower house of parliament.

Kesri, who became Congress party president in September when Rao stepped down under pressure, beat back a youthful challenge for the party's parliamentary leadership post from former cabinet minister Rajesh Pilot, who had earlier won backing from Rao loyalists.
"The consensus is in favour of Sitaram Kesri," former finance minister Manmohan Singh told the CPP meeting.
Rao, who was prime minister from 1991 until last May and spearheaded a drive to open up India's economy, quit under pressure as CPP leader last month.

On Thursday, Pilot, 51, had said he wanted a secret ballot to choose a new parliamentary leader. But former cabinet minister G. Venkatswamy said Kesri had been unanimously elected by the CPP, which has 225 members.
Congress, which has led India for all but four years since independence in 1947, suffered its worst ever defeat in general elections last year.

Rao had stepped down as Congress party president in September after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court to face criminal cheating charges. Kesri was named to succeed Rao at the head of India's oldest party.
The case is one of three criminal proceedings involving the taciturn, 75-year-old Rao, who claims he is innocent of the charges, each of which carries a maximum penalty of seven years in jail.
Rao had clung to his CPP post despite mounting opposition from Congress members keen to revamp the party's tarnished image.
But Rao bowed to the inevitable as supporters deserted him in the face of a campaign to overhaul the party's leadership.
